svg.title: How an LLM turns your words into its next word
svg.desc: One sentence through every stage of a tiny LLM. 1, text: "I went to bank to deposit". 2, tokens: I, went, to, bank, to, deposit. 3, GPT-2 token IDs: 40, 1816, 284, 3331, 284, 14667; both "to" tokens share ID 284. 4, each ID picks a row of numbers, its token embedding. 5, a small position vector is added to each row, giving the input: 6 rows of 4 numbers (GPT-2 uses 768). 6, inside the transformer block, after a norm, attention lets each word look back: "deposit" looks at "bank" with 34% of its attention, while "bank" cannot look ahead at "deposit". 7, attention’s output is added, then a norm and the feed-forward layer, and that output is added too: "deposit"’s money slot grows from 0.80 to 0.96 to 2.65. 8, a final norm, a score for each candidate word, and softmax: money 65%, cash 26%, some 4%, my 3%, the 2%, river 0.3%. The model picks "money", appends it, and runs again.
svg.text: How an LLM turns your words into its next word
“I went to bank to deposit” through every stage of a (tiny) LLM, until it predicts the next word.
I went to bank to deposit
I went to bank to deposit
A toy model: 4 numbers per token with named slots (money, place, action, grammar). GPT-2 uses 768 unnamed numbers. IDs are GPT-2’s.
